newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea shares close up 2.35 pct on strong yen/dlr.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea shares close up 2.35 pct on strong yen/dlr.

text.p: The strength of the yen against the dollar pushed South Korean stocks sharply higher on Thursday as investors bet that core manufacturing blue chips would benefit, traders and brokers said.
The composite price index ended trading on Thursday up 2.35 percent or 16.09 points to 699.95. This follows Tuesday's big rise of 1.75 percent. Wednesday was a market holiday.
The index briefly broke through the psychological barrier of 700 in early afternoon trading, then retreated.
Volume and value were heavy at 51.2 million shares and 742 billion won. Advancing shares swamped decliners by 544 to 252.

"I think a lot of people in the market have been waiting for something to be euphoric about," said Henry Morris, managing director of Coryo International (H.K.) Ltd, a securities firm. "This might have been the case of people clutching at the first straw that presented itself."
The yen has been firming against the dollar all week. In Tokyo trading, the yen stood at 116.27/30 against the dollar in mid-afternoon, after reaching 115.85/95 in late morning.
A strong yen makes Korean goods from autos to steel products more competitive in global markets.
"The yen's rise is boosting major manufacturing stocks, especially shipbuilding and other heavy-industrial sectors," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
The sub-index for large-cap stocks soared 3.26 percent.
Shares in five of the Daewoo Group's nine listed firms went limit-up, including Daewoo Heavy Industries, Daewoo Electronics, Daewoo Telecom, Daewoo Securities and Daewoo Corp.
"There's nothing particular going on with Daewoo shares," said S.W. Choi of Schroders Securities. "This is just speculative buying of low-priced, large-cap shares."
Most of the core blue chips ended the day well into positive territory.

Samsung Electronics was up 1,800 won to 63,600, while LG Electronics closed up 800 won to 11,400. Pohang Iron and Steel rose 1,300 won to 55,000, Hyundai Motor 67510.KS rose 1,400 won to 24.200 and Yukong
rose 1,200 won to 16,600.

The market shrugged off the news that the country's largest confectionery maker, Samlip General Foods Co, would seek court receivership. The stock exchange suspended trading of the company's shares from Thursday morning.
A statement from Samlip said the company had experienced financial problems because of "excessive investment and its payment guarantees on debts owed by its affiliates."
"The news that Samlip General Foods was having difficulties has been known, so there was no real impact," said Casey Choe, trader for Union Bank of Switzerland.

Investors also shrugged off the start of questioning of presidential son Kim Hyun-Chul by state prosecutors. Kim is suspected of taking kickbacks and peddling influence. Prosecution sources said Kim soon would be arrested.
Traders said the news of Kim had been reflected in the market and that, in the absence of any new developments, was unlikely to influence investor sentiment.
